initiative.title: Coax: the language and its toolchain, R0 to R12
initiative.body: The main Coax roadmap: what gets built in what order so OpenAgents and Metareal can express computation, data, protocols, tools and build policy in Coax, with costs and ownership visible. Milestones have dependencies and exit evidence, not dates.

milestones.title: R0: the adoption gate
milestones.body: Real engine kernels and the whole development loop measured against frozen references, original-source debugging, one release/status source and an independently enforced review gate. Exit: reproducible kernel and whole-loop reports, no unexpected output or allocation regressions, usable native debugging, a versioned baseline.

milestones.title: R1: the compiler substrate
milestones.body: R1a first: declaration and content identities, explicit targets, original spans, basic namespaces and inspectable procedure lowering, pinned by differential fixtures. R1b scheduling and configuration follow.

milestones.title: R2: fallible application code
milestones.body: R2a first: tagged results and optionals, exhaustive switching, propagation and cleanup; a shared asynchronous host contract with R3.

milestones.title: R3: ownership and allocation policies
milestones.body: R3a started (E0383 rejects simple returns of borrows into local arrays). Then typed transfer, deferred destruction and owning storage (R3b).

milestones.title: R4: generics and foundational libraries
milestones.body: R4a first: generic copyable values and non-owning operations over fixed storage; owning libraries wait for R3b.

milestones.title: R5: source-aware reflection and derivation
milestones.body: R5a first: narrow derivation over concrete, already-checked types.

milestones.title: R6: hygienic typed code and data transformations
milestones.body: Phase-typed Code, quotation, #insert and #expand with hygiene and expansion budgets.

milestones.title: R7: workspaces, plugins and tooling
milestones.body: R7a: formatting, evidence, typed queries and revision-bound fixes early, on current APIs. R7b: workspaces, typed plugins and build programming.

milestones.title: R8: the native GPU and browser path
milestones.body: R8a target-specific GPU interfaces; R8b a browser vertical slice (Coaxial is the wasm32 probe).

milestones.title: R9: effects, strict math and deterministic jobs
milestones.body: Transitive effect summaries for allocation, host I/O, clocks and randomness; strict math; deterministic jobs.

milestones.title: R10: self-hosting and the supported toolchain
milestones.body: The remaining semantic work moves into Coax in reviewable slices.

milestones.title: R11: resident compiler and transactional reload
milestones.body: R11a restricted procedure-body replacement (unchanged-layout Mac experiment first); R11b resident semantics and transactional migration.

milestones.title: R12: backends after profiling
milestones.body: The C backend stays the reference; a fast native debug backend only when profiling shows C compilation is the bottleneck.

tasks.title: Run eligible checks on emitted native code
tasks.body:
An optional native check executable runs pinned inputs through the evaluator and the emitted unoptimized and optimized procedures and compares values, traps and buffer writes.

Roadmap: coax/ROADMAP.md.

## Usage audit scope

Current differential probes cover a generated bounded grammar. They do not execute arbitrary eligible authored checks from the actual product files on emitted native code.

Implement the optional runner described above and use it on a documented eligible subset of real Verse and Psionic checks. Compare evaluator, checked native `-O0` and checked native `-O2` results, including returned values, specified traps, caller-buffer writes and cleanup. Report unsupported/unexecuted checks explicitly and keep shipping test code separate from product artifacts.

## Usage audit remaining scope

This issue includes both the core optional native-check runner and its real consumer qualification. The existing small differential grammar does not establish this broader support or general compiler correctness; GPU execution remains separate. Additional eligible syntax needs its own explicit evidence.
acceptance: Seeded evaluator/emitter defects are caught
Mismatches minimised and kept as regressions
An explicit native-check consumer command runs the same selected authored checks through evaluator, checked `-O0` and checked `-O2`, retaining target/profile identities.
Seeded evaluator/emitter defects produce nonzero counterexample outcomes; timeouts, unavailable tools and unsupported checks cannot produce passed outcomes.
Returned values, guard bytes, expected traps and cleanup writes are checked independently; test code is absent from normal product emission.
The record names eligible, rejected and unselected checks instead of treating omitted work as covered.

acceptance: coax test and coax mutate write the record

tasks.title: R1a: declaration identities, targets, spans and namespaces
tasks.body:
Declaration and content identities, explicit target descriptions, original spans, basic namespaces and minimal inspectable procedure lowering, pinned with differential fixtures and independent oracles.

Roadmap: coax/ROADMAP.md.

## Usage audit scope

A loaded graph has one declaration namespace. Psionic mesh entry points already compose more than one hundred physical units, while Verse and libraries must hand-prefix symbols. Shared source identity, native ABI identity and same-spelling declarations need distinct rules.

Deliver the namespace/identity portion of existing umbrella `r1a-identities` through the parser, checked graph and emitters. Specify explicit logical module IDs, private/public declarations, qualified lookup, reexports if supported, and their content/dependency identities before implementing syntax. Preserve physical-file authority and original spans. Establish the minimal inspectable shared procedure-lowering contract needed by these declarations; do not add a competing semantic frontend. Migrate one existing Verse or Psionic source graph and publish its dependency/identity report.

## Usage audit remaining scope

This is a substantial implementation contract, not completion by adding a header hash or a namespace parser alone. If it exceeds the owner's two-hour task limit, create linked acceptance-complete subtasks before implementation and keep this task open until all listed behavior lands. Packages, network fetching, privileged builds and general incremental compilation remain separate. The broader `r1a-identities` umbrella closes only on its own full acceptance.
acceptance: Differential fixtures pass against independent oracles

`python3 coax/tests/modules.py` covers private access refusal, duplicate logical IDs, qualified collisions, dependency cycles, content changes, shared declaration identity and original-source diagnostics.
`python3 coax/tests/sources.py` and affected checker/seed gates pass; authority requirements survive composition.
The selected real graph builds and its existing checks run with its authored behavior unchanged; its unit count, exposed names, source/content IDs and generated sizes are retained.
Deterministic regeneration and the affected evaluator/C/GPU lowering fixtures agree on the same checked declaration identities.

tasks.title: R7a: a formatter and evidence tools on current APIs
tasks.body:
coax fmt and evidence reporting using today's compiler APIs; typed queries and revision-bound fixes follow R1a.

Roadmap: coax/ROADMAP.md.

## Usage audit scope

Agents copy inconsistent syntax layout and spend review effort on mechanical changes. A canonical formatter is still missing despite machine-readable diagnostics and a shared checked frontend.

Implement the concrete formatter portion of existing `r7a-format-evidence` using current syntax/source APIs. Preserve comments, literal bytes, directives, physical-file boundaries and authored source ranges; provide check mode and revision-safe writes. Exercise Verse, Psionic and compiler graphs without automatically rewriting unrelated repository files.

## Usage audit remaining scope

This is a concrete slice of `r7a-format-evidence`; evidence tools, typed queries and compiler-service/LSP operation remain separate. Do not close the existing umbrella solely because formatter idempotence passes. Split the implementation if needed to respect the owner's task limit.
acceptance: coax fmt is idempotent over the repository's Coax files
`python3 coax/tests/format.py` verifies idempotence, preserved comments/literals, refused malformed input, stale-write refusal and no modifications in check mode.
All supported repository Coax sources format twice identically in a temporary corpus.
Parsed/checked semantic output and eligible native behavior of frozen before/after fixtures agree.
No unrelated product source formatting is included in the implementation commit.

tasks.title: R2a: tagged results, optionals and exhaustive switching
tasks.body:
Typed results and optionals, exhaustive switch, propagation and exhaustive cleanup, with one real asynchronous adapter.

Roadmap: coax/ROADMAP.md.

## Usage audit scope

Receiving an error/value struct does not force the caller to inspect its error. Real clients separately track status, body, problem, completion and retained buffers, allowing invalid combinations.

Deliver a concrete consumer of umbrella `r2a-results`: tagged success/refusal/cancellation/unknown outcomes, exhaustive switching and cleanup on every exit. Specify inactive-payload access and propagation semantics before implementation. Migrate one existing asynchronous System One, gateway or voice request adapter and preserve its remote idempotency/reconciliation rules.

## Usage audit remaining scope

The existing `r2a-results` issue remains the language umbrella. A single consumer or tagged struct is not completion of optionals, exhaustive switching, propagation and cleanup. Split this work into linked tasks when necessary; retain missing language forms as open work rather than closing the umbrella.
acceptance: The spec's R2a examples compile and their checks pass
`python3 coax/tests/results.py` rejects nonexhaustive cases and inactive-payload access and covers nested propagation, early return and reverse-order cleanup.
The same result/cleanup vectors agree in evaluator and checked native `-O0`/`-O2` execution.
The selected adapter's existing success, refusal, late-completion, duplicate-completion and cancellation traces pass; unknown remote outcomes never trigger an unsafe automatic retry.
Relevant authority checks and mutation gates pass without equivalent-mutation exemptions.
